title: Top VC on Palantir: “You Literally Can’t Stop Your Margins Going Up”
detail:
Top VC on Palantir: “You Literally Can’t Stop Your Margins Going Up”
Michael Douglass
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 8:20 AM MST 4 min read
PLTR
Trade PLTR on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Top VC on Palantir: "You Literally Can't Stop Your Margins Going Up" ©@Mungkhoodstudio's Images via Canva, @aukidphumsirichat via Canva
Key Takeaways

Scale Venture Partners' Rory O'Driscoll said on 20VC that Palantir's multimillion-dollar contracts let revenue grow faster than the company can hire, so its margins keep rising.

Palantir's operating margin went from -26.7% in 2021 to 31.6% in 2025 and about 47% in the third quarter of 2026, and revenue per employee has roughly doubled.

The main risk is new business: total contract value grew just 6% in the third quarter, and analysts expect revenue growth to slow to about 53% in 2027.

Palantir trades at 75x forward earnings, well under its three-year average of 130x, and its first 2027 guidance in early February is the next test.

Palantir Technologies (PLTR:NASDAQ) has had a rough few weeks. AI stocks sold off, and the stock fell about 18% from its Oct. 9 closing high, even though third-quarter revenue grew 96% to $2.31 billion.

The selloff didn't change the basic math of how Palantir makes money, though. On this week's episode of 20VC, Scale Venture Partners' Rory O'Driscoll pointed to how much revenue Palantir brings in for each person it employs:

"Palantir at 2 million, 2 million per employee. It's very enterprise, but it's 2 million per employee, growing 100%, growing 98%."

Then he explained why that matters: "if you have $2 and $5 million contracts like Palantir, and if revenue doubles, you probably can't hire headcount fast enough to catch up. You literally can't stop your margins going up, which is a wonderful place to be."

That's about as bullish as a margin argument gets.

TIKR tracks 33 analysts on Palantir. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Palantir, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Palantir's Analyst Ratings

The numbers back him up

Palantir's revenue doubled in two years, from $2.23 billion in 2023 to $4.48 billion in 2025. Analysts expect $8.55 billion this year and $19.2 billion by 2028:

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2023-2028 (TIKR)

Headcount hasn't kept up. Palantir's annual report says it ended 2025 with 4,429 full-time employees. Multiply the third quarter's $2.31 billion by four and you get about $9.2 billion, or roughly $2 million per employee. (That assumes headcount is still close to where it ended 2025, since Palantir gives the count only once a year.) Over all of 2025, it brought in about $1 million per employee.

As that gap has opened up, the operating margin has climbed every year, from -26.7% in 2021 to 31.6% in 2025:

Palantir Technologies (PLTR): operating (EBIT) margin (%), fiscal 2021-2025 (TIKR)

The margin is higher still now: $1.08 billion of operating income in the third quarter, about 47% of revenue.

CorpGov hosted the sixth annual Palm Beach CorpGov Forum on Nov. 4-5, 2026, at the Palm Beach Lake Pavilion and The Cove Club, both located waterfront with sweeping views of Palm Beach Island, along with a reception at Cucina Palm Beach. The panel called "AI Governance for Boards" took place on Thursday afternoon.

The panel featured Doug Chia, President, Soundboard Governance; Host, The Public Company Series Podcast; Former Corporate Secretary of Johnson & Johnson, and George Corbin, Board Director, Edgewell Personal Care (NYSE: EPC); Former Chief Digital Officer at Marriott and Mars. Robert Maciejko, Founder, Board AI Institute; Co-founder, INSEAD AI (Alum-Led); Member of INSEAD's AI Advisory Group, moderated the discussion. 

Key comments from the panel:

"I've always thought that the biggest soft spot in corporate governance, no matter where we are in the United States, is the information gap, information asymmetry between management and the board," stated Doug Chia.

"Boards are, as they're kind of wired to do, over-indexing for risk and productivity from AI and under-indexing on strategic growth, the growth questions that can come from AI," said George Corbin.

"83% of boards say that AI is material for their business," mentioned Robert Maciejko. "Now, what percent of board directors do you think are AI experts according to their declarations and SEC filings? 5%."

Palantir CTO Shyam Sankar filed to sell 300,000 shares worth about $51 million, a tiny 0.013% slice of shares outstanding.

Sankar adopted his 10b5-1 selling plan in August, three months before the selloff, so the sale signals little about his view of the stock.

Palantir's revenue jumped 96% and guidance rose, yet the stock still fell, pointing to valuation, not business results, as the culprit.

The biggest 401k decisions tend to get made once and never revisited: when to roll it over, what to hold inside it, and when to start taking money out. That is exactly what the report: 401k & IRA Tips and Answers was created to address, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Shyam Sankar, the chief technology officer of Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR), filed to sell 300,000 shares. The SEC accepted his Form 144 notice at 4:26 p.m. ET on November 10, 2026. It lists a total market value of $50,760,000, names Morgan Stanley Smith Barney as broker and gives November 10 as the approximate sale date.

24/7 Wall St.

The filing came after a sharp fall. Palantir fell 9.73% on November 5, the day the S&P 500 dropped 4.36% in the AI and chip selloff. That drop ended eight straight down sessions that began October 27.

The shares have recovered since then. They rose 5.50% on November 9, slipped 0.22% on November 10, and gained 2.12% to close at $172.40 on November 11. That close is still 17.53% below the October 9 closing high of $209.05, and the stock was trading at $169.80 after hours.

What Sankar's Form 144 Actually Commits To

A Form 144 states an intent to sell. A later Form 4 will confirm whether any shares were sold and at what prices.

The shares came from restricted stock units, which are stock grants that turn into shares as they vest. These units vested between May 20, 2025, and August 20, 2025, and the notice reports no Palantir sales by Sankar in the prior three months.

More on the Anthropic IPO: our Anthropic IPO storyline page collects our pieces on it.

Your company probably switched on an AI assistant this year. Someone had to decide which files it may read and who checks its answers. That wiring is what Palantir sells; its US business customers reached 686 in the third quarter, up 29%.

Next week the company behind one of those assistants is set to go public. Anthropic, the maker of Claude, plans to price its IPO around November 18, CNBC reported, at $70 to $78 a share, about $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion fully diluted. Next to Anthropic, is Palantir the pricier AI stock?

Yes, by a wide margin. On its November 2 earnings call, Palantir's management said AI's value is flowing to very few companies, naming Anthropic next to itself. Now Anthropic lists. Its September-quarter revenue was $16.96 billion, 7.3 times Palantir's $2.31 billion and about twice Palantir's whole 2026 forecast of $8.53 billion.

Sales 7.3 times Palantir's make ANT hard to ignore. In a portfolio of a few million dollars, Palantir, Nvidia and index funds may form one big AI bet. How much would ANT add? A Trefis partner firm can tally it in a free 15-minute call.

title: Palantir Grew Revenue 96%. The Stock Fell 5%. Here's What I'm Doing.
detail:
Palantir Grew Revenue 96%. The Stock Fell 5%. Here's What I'm Doing.
Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool
Thu, November 12, 2026 at 2:15 AM MST 3 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) reported very strong earnings once again on Nov. 2. The highlight of the release was its accelerating 96% revenue growth. However, the market didn't love the results, and the stock sold off more than 10% in the days following earnings.

The stock has rebounded some, but recently was still down 5% from its price before earnings were released. Overall, Palantir is down around 20% from its all-time high, so some investors may be viewing this as a buying opportunity.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

But what am I doing? I'm still staying patient. Palantir is a great business that's growing remarkably fast, but there's one huge holdup that keeps me from purchasing shares, and it could be some time before I decide to open a position.

Image source: The Motley Fool.
Palantir is pricey for its growth

At face value, Palantir's AI analytics business is doing fantastic. Its revenue is soaring, and it has 49% profit margins. The business is strong, and so is its outlook, so what's not to love about this stock? It all comes down to the price tag.

The best companies bought at the wrong price can still be bad investments, and that's exactly how I view Palantir's stock. Palantir trades at about 100 times this year's earnings and 67 times next year's earnings.

PLTR PE Ratio (Forward) data by YCharts

For reference, I can buy other AI stocks, like Nvidia or Alphabet, which trade at 11 and 19 times next year's earnings, respectively. These two are stalwarts in the industry, yet trade at huge discounts. Palantir's growth will be dedicated to reducing its valuation over the next few years, while Nvidia and Alphabet are cheap enough that every bit of growth they deliver should result in a corresponding rise in their stock.

That makes the long-term prospects for these two (and countless other AI investments) far stronger. As a result, I'm OK passing on Palantir. There are many great AI investments, and you don't have to invest in them all. The day of reckoning for Palantir's stock valuation could be coming soon, as it has maintained its high valuation even while many other AI stocks have seen their valuation premiums erased. Time will tell, but right now it seems like a precarious time to be a Palantir investor, with so many other great deals available in AI stocks.
